content.content:
Tilts-The-Jug: "There is, if the hands are careful enough. The Chapter takes from those who can bear the loss. It takes no more than that. A hand that breaks what it touches is no use to us, so I must see how yours work. Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of this door. He took a necklace of polished blue jaspers from a Lookout of ours, one of the Chapter, while that Lookout slept. He keeps it in a locked strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. Bring the necklace back, so that the Lookout has it again. Do Keeps-What-Floats no harm. If he is hurt, there is no pay and no place with us. Here are three lockpicks. There are three ways open. You can open his strongbox with the picks, or you can take his key, which he may give for good talk or sell for coin. Sits-By-The-Water drinks with him on the dock. Ask her about his habits, because I will not tell them."

content.text:
I ran out of commands before the game finished, so I stopped partway through the second quest.

- **Quest 1, "A Dry Hand in a Wet City":** S'Tabi sent me to Tilts-The-Jug, who told me to get a stolen necklace back from Keeps-What-Floats without hurting him. I couldn't afford the 60 gold for his key, and persuading him failed. So I picked the strongbox lock and chose "seen", because everyone was standing around. Tilts-The-Jug paid me 100 gold and sent me to Lilmoth, where Bent-Spine made me a Lookout in the Night-Reed Chapter.
- **Quest 2, "The Drowned Lockbox":** I opened the drowned merchant's lockbox and took all three pledges. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel each claim one. My attempt to sell Neeta-Haj the figurine at full price failed, so I sold it to her for 20 gold. I still hold the Neesak charm and the glass beads. The quest is still open: the next step is to sell Okan-Tei the charm.

I gave the game my take with `play end`. I said the quests were clear, the Chapter's "take from those who can bear the loss" rule gave the jobs some moral weight, and I wanted to see how the charm sale plays out. I also flagged three problems. The "seen" lockpicking prompt had no follow-up, my failed persuasion gave no hint how to improve, and the journal said I had not pressed Neeta-Haj.
